question: What's the difference between a Residency License and an Initial Professional License?

answer.summary: A residency license is a one-year license, renewable twice, that a public school unit requests for an applicant under its employment, and it carries required renewal documentation and professional development. An initial professional license is a three-year nonrenewable license that entitles the holder to practice as an independent professional educator, and a residency license can be converted to one by June 30 of its third year.

claims.text: A residency license is a one-year license, renewable twice, issued to an individual who meets the qualifications of LICN-019.
An initial professional license (IPL) is a three-year, nonrenewable license issued to an applicant or professional educator who meets the relevant requirements established by SBE policy.
An IPL entitles the licensee to practice as an independent professional educator in North Carolina.

To request a residency license, the applicant must meet the requirements of G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(5) and have either completed at least 24 hours of coursework in the content area or passed the applicable licensure examination requirements for that content area. The request is made by the governing body of a public school unit or eligible nonpublic school for an applicant under its employment.

To renew a residency license for a given year, the employing school unit must document that the applicant is enrolled in a recognized educator preparation program, is employed as a teacher in that unit, acquired at least six months of teaching experience during the preceding school year, and completed 10 days of professional development in the first year of the residency license.

To convert a residency license to an IPL or CPL, the applicant must meet the IPL or CPL requirements and be recommended by the educator preparation program that prepared the licensee. If the requirements are met by June 30 of the third year of the residency license, the IPL or CPL takes effect July 1 of the next fiscal year; otherwise the residency license expires and the IPL or CPL takes effect when the requirements are met.
A person who holds or previously held a residency license is not eligible for a permit to teach or an emergency license in the same license area.

A public school unit employing a residency license holder must provide at least three hours of field experience before classroom teaching and at least 10 hours over the first year, plus 10 days of professional development (or the alternative training in LICN-019 §5(d)).

An out-of-state applicant with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for an IPL by holding a license in the corresponding area in another jurisdiction or by completing a recognized educator preparation program.

not_covered: The full eligibility requirements for an in-state IPL under LICN-020 (only the license's effect in LICN-020 §3 was provided).
Whether a residency license holder may hold an IPL in a different license area, beyond the additional-area provisions in LICN-019 §4.
The content of the statutes cited (G.S. 115C-270.20) and the CPL requirements referenced in the conversion rule (LICN-024 was not provided).
Any rules that applied before the 2026-07-01 effective date of these policies.

metrics.judge_rationale: The answer gets the core difference right: residency license is one-year renewable twice, IPL is three-year nonrenewable, and conversion and renewal rules are accurate and well cited. It omits the in-state EPP-recommendation IPL path, the exam-only IPL route for a PSU request, the add-on area rule, and the CPL link, so it is incomplete rather than wrong.

question: What's the difference between an IPL and a CPL in NC?

answer.summary: An IPL is a three-year, nonrenewable license for a educator who is new or has fewer than three years of experience, while a CPL is a five-year renewable license that requires a three-year track record, exam requirements, and a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless an exception applies. Both let the holder practice as an independent professional educator in North Carolina.

claims.text: An IPL is a three-year, nonrenewable license issued to an applicant or professional educator who meets the relevant SBE policy requirements.
A CPL is a five-year, renewable license issued to an applicant or professional educator who meets the relevant SBE policy requirements.
An IPL entitles the licensee to practice as an independent professional educator in North Carolina.
A CPL also entitles the licensee to practice as an independent professional educator in North Carolina.

A teacher can qualify for an IPL by completing a recognized North Carolina educator preparation program and being recommended by the EPP, or by completing an out-of-state EPP, or by holding a clear out-of-state license and having fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction.

To qualify for a teacher CPL, an applicant must hold an IPL or residency license in North Carolina, satisfy licensure examination requirements before or during the third year of licensure, have at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and complete a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless they have three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina or previously held a CPL that reverted to an IPL.

Teachers employed by a local board of education must have evidence of a rating of at least proficient on their most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL, meaning a rating of Proficient or higher on three of the five NC Professional Teaching Standards, including Standard 4.

A CPL can revert to an IPL. If a teacher on a CPL in the final year of a renewal cycle is not deemed proficient, the LSAU may place them on a mandatory improvement plan, and if the teacher otherwise meets requirements, DPI issues an IPL. The reversion is not a demotion and does not reduce salary.
A reverted IPL has a three-year term, after which the teacher may apply for a CPL if they meet the requirements, including CEU completion.
A CPL remains in effect for five years after the licensee retires from full-time employment as a professional educator.
An out-of-state applicant may not use out-of-state exam results to convert an IPL to a CPL.

question: Applicant with a CPL from Maryland in middle school science, moved to NC and is now teaching high school chemistry. Does the MD license cover HS chem or is an add-on needed?

answer.summary: The Maryland license does not carry over to high school chemistry by itself: NC coverage depends on the areas printed on the NC license, and a middle grades science area is a different classification from Secondary chemistry. Chemistry can be added through a passing out-of-state chemistry exam submitted at initial NC application, or after issuance through the LICN-013 exam or 24-credit-hour route, so the answer turns on whether a chemistry exam was passed and when it was submitted.

claims.text: A teacher license entitles the licensee to teach only in the license area(s) indicated on that license.

Middle Grades Science and Secondary Chemistry are listed as separate license classifications in the NC license framework, so a middle grades science area does not on its face include Secondary (9-12) chemistry.

An out-of-state applicant who qualifies for a teacher license under LICN-025 Sections 1 or 2 may request to add a teaching license area based solely on a passing score on an out-of-state exam in that area, provided the exam results are submitted at the time of the initial NC license application.
If the out-of-state applicant seeks to add a teaching area after the NC license has been issued, the applicant must follow the LICN-013 requirements.
Under LICN-013, an applicant may add a teaching area to an IPL or CPL only if the applicant has met the licensure examination requirements for the initial license area.

Under LICN-013, a teaching area may be added by satisfying the applicable licensure examination requirements for that area, or by completing 24 credit hours of coursework from an institution of higher education in the license area with a grade of C or better in each course.
Secondary Chemistry (license code 330) uses NC test code 5246 with a required score of 146 under the NC approved testing table.
The out-of-state applicant may not use out-of-state exam results to convert an IPL to a CPL, and out-of-state exam evidence must be presented at initial licensure in NC.

Chemistry is not among the license areas that LICN-013 §2 bars from being added by coursework alone (that list covers Elementary Education and Exceptional Children: General Curriculum only), so the coursework route is not excluded for chemistry.

Because the MD license is out-of-state, its own coverage in Maryland is not what governs NC teaching; the NC license areas control, and the MD middle grades science area does not appear on the NC license as chemistry.

question: Is there a Limited License for teachers, and when is it used?

answer.summary: Yes. North Carolina has a Limited License for teachers. It is a three-year renewable license for someone who completed an educator preparation program but has not yet passed the required licensure exam, and it is used either when a school unit requests it for an applicant under its employment who meets G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(4a), or for a previous lateral-entry license holder who is currently employed and meets the affidavit conditions. The passages do not spell out the statutory criteria, so those must be checked against the statute.

claims.text: A Limited License is one of the teacher license classifications.
A Limited License is defined as a three-year renewable license issued to an individual who has completed an EPP but has not satisfied the applicable licensure examination requirements.

A governing body of a public school unit may request a limited license for an applicant under its employment if the applicant meets the requirements of G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(4a). A limited license may only be issued for teaching license areas, not for administrator or student services personnel license areas.

A person who previously held a lateral entry license under G.S. 115C-297 (repealed by S.L. 2017-189), and who meets all IPL or CPL requirements except passing the licensure examination for that area, qualifies for a limited license if the person is currently employed by the PSU governing body and the PSU submits a signed affidavit from the superintendent (or equivalent) and the principal stating that the person is currently employed, is an effective teacher, and will be encouraged to pursue an IPL or CPL.

To renew a limited license, the employing PSU must submit an affidavit from the supervising principal and local superintendent attesting that the licensee is currently employed, is an effective teacher, and that the PSU will encourage the licensee to pursue a CPL.

To renew, the licensee must meet or exceed expected growth as measured by EVAAS where data is available. If more than one year of growth data exists, DPI averages it. Data is limited to years since the limited license was first issued or its most recent renewal, and DPI does not consider 2019-2020 or 2020-2021 EVAAS data.
A limited license cannot be transferred from one PSU to another, except for military service members and spouses covered by LICN-028.
Limited Licenses are not eligible for added teaching areas (add-on areas).

question: How long is a Residency License valid and can it be extended?

answer.summary: The passages do not state a single explicit validity period for a Residency License, but they show it runs through a three-year timeframe, with renewal documentation required for the second and third years and conversion due by June 30 of the third year. They do not provide a general extension; the only route back is reinstatement under LICN-019 §2(b), and only if the conditions there are met.

claims.text: A residency license is treated as a three-year license: the policy refers to renewal 'for the second or third year' and requires conversion by June 30 of the third year of the residency license.

To renew a residency license, the employing PSU or eligible nonpublic school must document to DPI that the applicant is enrolled in a recognized EPP, is employed as a teacher there, acquired at least six months of teaching experience during the preceding school year, and (in the first year) completed 10 days of professional development.
If the applicant fails to renew for the second or third year, the residency license expires.

Reinstatement is possible: a PSU that hires the applicant within three years of the initial residency license's effective date may ask DPI to reinstate it, provided the license has not already been renewed twice and the PSU documents that the applicant is employed by it and enrolled in a recognized EPP.

If the applicant meets the conversion requirements (IPL or CPL requirements and EPP recommendation) by June 30 of the third year, the IPL or CPL is effective July 1 of the next fiscal year; if not, the residency license expires and the IPL or CPL is effective when requirements are met.

For a servicemember or spouse pursuing a residency license who is called to active duty or relocated outside North Carolina, the three-year timeframe is held in abeyance until the servicemember returns to North Carolina and returns to employment in a North Carolina public school.
The 'cannot be extended or renewed' rule appears in the permit to teach and emergency license policies, not in the residency license policy, so it does not directly govern residency licenses.
Under the general rule, every license expires June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire unless renewed, extended, or converted under SBE policy.

question: What's the process to move from an RL to an IPL?

answer.summary: To convert a residency license (RL) to an IPL, the applicant must meet the IPL requirements in LICN-020 and be recommended by the EPP that prepared them. If that is done by June 30 of the RL's third year, the IPL takes effect July 1 of the next fiscal year; if not, the RL expires and the IPL takes effect on the date requirements are met.

claims.text: To convert a residency license to an IPL or CPL, the applicant must meet the requirements for an IPL in LICN-020 (or a CPL in LICN-024) and be recommended by the EPP that prepared the licensee.

Under LICN-020, an IPL qualification is met by completing a recognized NC EPP and being recommended by that EPP for the requested license, or by completing an EPP outside NC, or by holding a clear out-of-state license with fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction.
Timing: if the applicant satisfies the requirements by June 30 of the third year of the residency license, the IPL is effective July 1 of the next fiscal year.
Timing: if the applicant does not satisfy the requirements by June 30 of the third year, the residency license expires and the IPL is effective on the date the applicant satisfies the requirements.

If the applicant is a servicemember or military spouse who is called to active duty or relocated by military orders outside NC while pursuing a residency license, the three-year timeframe for completing the EPP and other IPL/CPL requirements is held in abeyance until the servicemember returns to NC and returns to employment in a NC public school.

question: What are the requirements for a CPL in terms of years of experience and renewal cycle?

answer.summary: For a teacher to qualify for a continuing professional license (CPL), the passages require at least three years of licensed teaching experience, plus the other conditions in LICN-024. A CPL is renewed every five years, and teachers must complete eight CEUs in each renewal cycle.

claims.text: To qualify for a teacher CPL, an applicant must hold an initial professional educator license or residency license in North Carolina, and must have at least three years of licensed teaching experience.

A teacher CPL also requires satisfying the licensure examination requirements, and completing a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless the applicant has at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina or previously held a CPL that reverted to an IPL.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a CPL, if the applicant also meets the clear-license criteria and either holds National Board certification or has licensure requirements substantially similar to North Carolina's.
A CPL is a five-year, renewable license.
Each teacher holding a CPL must renew that license every five years.

Within each five-year renewal cycle, a teacher in Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5 must complete eight CEUs, and a teacher in Grades 6 through 12 must also complete eight CEUs (four in the license area and four general).
Administrators and student services personnel also renew their CPLs every five years, with eight CEUs required in each renewal cycle.

The passages do not state a years-of-experience requirement for administrator or student services personnel CPLs. LICN-024 §2 requires only examination requirements and the requirements of LICN-011 or LICN-012.

not_covered: Whether the three-year licensed teaching experience must be completed before or during the license period, or how partial years are counted, is not addressed in the passages.
The experience requirements that apply to administrator and student services personnel CPLs are not stated in the passages provided (LICN-011 and LICN-012 are referenced but not included).
The requirements for the Beginning Teacher Support Program (TCED-016) are referenced but not included.
The passages are current versions only (effective 2026-07-01); they do not confirm what rules applied before that date.

It omits the LEA proficient-rating requirement and the CEU definition, and it labels the verdict as informational without asking for the license classification or grade band that the key says are needed for a definitive answer.

question: How many CEUs are needed to renew a CPL, and do any have to be in a specific area?

answer.summary: The number of CEUs and whether any must be in a specific area depend on the license holder's role and, for teachers, grade band. Teachers need 8 CEUs every five years, with 3 or 4 in the license area depending on grade band, and administrators and student services personnel also need 8 with a role-specific portion. Please confirm the role and grade band before giving a final count.

claims.text: A CPL must be renewed every five years by teachers, administrators, and student services personnel under their respective renewal policies.

Teachers in Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5 must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: three in the teacher's license area (consistent with Standards 3 and 4), three related to literacy, and two general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment.

Teachers in Grades 6 through 12 must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: four in the teacher's license area (consistent with Standards 3 and 4) and four general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. No literacy-specific CEUs are listed for this grade band.

Administrators must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: four focused on the administrator's leadership role in instruction, human resources, and management, and four general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment.

Student services personnel must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: four that align with the North Carolina standards for their professional discipline as outlined in the EVAL policy series, and four general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment.
School audiologists and school speech-language pathologists are exempt from the CEU requirements while they continue to satisfy the applicable LICN-012 requirements.

One CEU equals either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from a higher education institution or ten clock hours of professional development programming. Eight CEUs therefore equal about 5.33 semester credit hours (8 × 2/3) or 80 clock hours (8 × 10).

A teacher who receives National Board Certification receives credit for all eight CEUs in the renewal cycle in which the certification is received. A teacher who renews National Board Certification receives credit for two CEUs in that cycle.

Hours in mandatory training programs count toward CEUs only if the training is required by State law or by a local board as a condition of employment, and the educator has otherwise met the renewal requirements for the license type.
Teachers employed by a local board must also have evidence of a rating of at least proficient on their most recent annual evaluation, with proficiency on Standard 4, to renew a CPL.

question: How does reinstatement work for a license that expired a few years ago?

answer.summary: The provided policies do not contain a general reinstatement process for an expired license. The 'reinstatement' petition in LICN-007 applies only to revoked licenses or denied applications, so it does not fit. Two narrower paths may apply depending on the license type and employment history: validation of an expired CPL requested by a PSU (LICN-033 §3), and reinstatement of a residency license within three years (LICN-019 §2(b)). The analyst needs to confirm the license type, how long it has been expired, and the educator's PSU employment history before an outcome can be stated.

claims.text: LICN-007 §8 provides a reinstatement petition only for an individual whose license has been revoked or whose application for a license has been denied. It does not address expired licenses.

Under LICN-007 §8(a), a petition may be submitted no sooner than 12 months after the effective date of the revocation or denial. Under §8(c), the Superintendent may deny, grant, or grant on probation, and a probationary grant is reviewed one year later.

Under LICN-001 §3(g), every license expires on June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire, unless it is renewed, extended, or converted in accordance with SBE policy. The passages do not describe a general reinstatement path for expired licenses beyond the specific provisions below.

For an expired continuing professional license (CPL), a PSU governing body may request that DPI validate the expired CPL for an educator under its employment, even if the educator lacks the required CEUs, but only if the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year.

A validated CPL is effective for three years. To renew it for a new five-year renewal cycle, the educator must complete the relevant renewal requirements in LICN-030, LICN-031, or LICN-032 by the end of the third year.

For a residency license that expired because the applicant did not renew it for the second or third year, a PSU or eligible nonpublic school that hires the applicant within three years of the effective date of the initial residency license may request that DPI reinstate it. Reinstatement requires that the license has not already been renewed twice, and documentation that the applicant is employed by the employing unit and enrolled in a recognized educator preparation program.

The passages do not state reinstatement or validation rules for expired initial professional licenses (IPLs), permits, or other license types, and do not state any time limit on reinstating an expired CPL.

question: What's the renewal deadline for a standard CPL, and what happens if it lapses?

answer.summary: A standard CPL is a five-year license, and the renewal deadline is the end of its five-year renewal cycle, but the passages do not give a calendar date. If a teacher employed by a local school administrative unit is not rated proficient, the outcome depends on whether the LSAU places the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan; if the teacher meets the requirements but is not placed on one, the license expires at the end of the cycle.

claims.text: A continuing professional license (CPL) is a five-year, renewable license issued to an applicant or professional educator who meets the relevant SBE policy requirements.
A renewal cycle is the five-year period between each renewal of a CPL.
Each teacher holding a CPL must renew that license every five years.
Each person holding a student services personnel license must renew that license every five years.

Teachers must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: Pre-K through Grade 5 teachers complete 3 license-area, 3 literacy, and 2 general CEUs; Grades 6-12 teachers complete 4 license-area and 4 general CEUs. Each renewal cycle therefore requires 8 CEUs in total.

A teacher employed by a local board of education must have evidence of a rating of at least "proficient" on the most recent annual evaluation in NCEES to renew a CPL. Proficient means a rating of Proficient or higher on three of the five NC Professional Teaching Standards, including Proficient on Standard 4.

If a teacher employed by a local board of education holds a current CPL, is in the final year of a renewal cycle, and was not deemed proficient, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan. If placed on the plan and the teacher otherwise meets licensure requirements, DPI shall issue an IPL.

If a teacher meets the Section 1 criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan by the employing LSAU, the teacher's license expires at the end of the renewal cycle. The teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving notice of expiration from DPI.

A PSU governing body may ask DPI to validate an expired CPL, even without the required CEUs, only if the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year. A validated CPL is effective for three years, and the educator must complete the renewal requirements by the end of the third year to renew for a new five-year cycle.
Reversion from a CPL to an IPL is not a demotion and does not reduce salary.

question: Is there a grace period after a license expires where someone can still renew?
context_ids: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

answer.summary: The policies provided do not establish a general grace period for renewing a license after it expires. They describe several narrower pathways (validation of an expired CPL, an IPL application window for certain teachers, and reinstatement of residency licenses), and which one applies depends on the license type and the educator's circumstances.

claims.text: Every license expires on June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire, unless it is renewed, extended, or converted to another type of license under SBE policy. The policies provided do not describe a renewal window that continues after that date.

A PSU governing body may ask DPI to validate an expired CPL for an applicant it employs, even without the required CEUs, if the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year. A validated CPL is effective for three years, and the educator must complete the renewal requirements in LICN-030, LICN-031, or LICN-032 by the end of the third year to renew for a new five-year cycle.

A teacher who meets the renewal criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan by the employing LSAU has the license expire at the end of the renewal cycle. That teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving notice of expiration from DPI.

If a teacher is placed on a mandatory improvement plan, DPI issues an IPL when the teacher otherwise meets licensure requirements. The plan runs 90 instructional days in low-performing schools and 60 instructional days in all other schools. At the end of the three-year IPL term, the teacher may apply for a CPL if the requirements, including required CEUs, are met.

For a residency license that is not renewed for the second or third year, the license expires. A PSU that hires the applicant within three years of the initial residency license's effective date may ask DPI to reinstate it, as long as the license has not already been renewed twice and the applicant is employed by the PSU and enrolled in a recognized educator preparation program.
An emergency license cannot be extended or renewed and is valid only until June 30 of the fiscal year for which it was requested.

question: Can a teacher teach a course outside their licensure area, and is there a time limit?

answer.summary: The provided LICN policies do not say whether a teacher may teach a course outside their licensure area or set any time limit for doing so. The policies only establish that a teacher license authorizes teaching in the license areas listed on it, and that a licensee can add a license area through an examination or coursework route.

claims.text: A teacher license entitles the licensee to teach in the license area(s) indicated on the license.
A 'license area' is a grade level, content area, or specialization in which a license authorizes the licensee to practice.

A licensee may add a new license area to an existing initial professional license or continuing professional license. A limited license may only be issued for teaching license areas. A limited license is a three-year renewable license for an individual who has completed an EPP but has not satisfied the applicable examination requirements.

question: How do you add a new licensure area to an existing NC license?
context_ids: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

answer.summary: An educator can add a new license area to an existing initial professional license (IPL) or continuing professional license (CPL) in one of two ways: by passing the required NC licensure exam for that area, or by completing 24 credit hours of higher-education coursework in that area with a grade of C or better in each course. Elementary Education and Exceptional Children: General Curriculum can be added only by passing the exam, and residency, permit, emergency, limited, provisional, international faculty, and CTE restricted licenses cannot have areas added under this policy.

claims.text: An applicant may request to add a new license area to an existing IPL or CPL.
An applicant may add a license area to an IPL only if the applicant has already met the licensure examination requirements for the initial license area.

To add an additional teaching area, the applicant must either satisfy the applicable licensure examination requirements for that area, or complete 24 credit hours of coursework from an institution of higher education in the license area and earn a grade of C or better in each course.
For Elementary Education and Exceptional Children: General Curriculum, the area may be added only by satisfying the licensure examination requirements; coursework alone is not permitted.
The Department shall not add teaching areas under this policy to Permit to Teach, Emergency, Residency, Limited, Provisional, International Faculty, or CTE Restricted licenses.

Exam requirements for many areas are listed in the approved testing table, with the Praxis code and required score for each area. Example: Art requires Praxis 5135 with a score of 161, and Music requires Praxis 5114 with a score of 162.

An out-of-state applicant with a teaching license may add an area based solely on a passing score on an out-of-state exam in that area, if the exam results are submitted with the initial North Carolina application. After a North Carolina license has been issued, the applicant must follow LICN-013.

A residency license holder may be granted a residency license in an additional area if employed by a public school unit and holding a clear license in another area, meeting G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(5). This is a separate route from adding an area to an IPL or CPL.

The fee schedule lists $60 for an individual to add an area by test or 24 semester hours, and $60 for an employing school system to add an alternative area. These fees are for applications opened effective January 1, 2017, and the schedule is dated 2018-04-05.

question: What are the testing requirements for adding a licensure area?

question: How does NC handle licensure for teachers coming from another state?

To obtain a continuing professional teacher license, an applicant must generally complete a Beginning Teacher Support Program, but this is not required if the applicant has at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina.

A continuing professional teacher license also requires holding an initial professional or residency license in North Carolina, at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and satisfying the licensure examination requirements before or during the third year of licensure.

question: Teacher says they hit exactly the minimum CEU count this cycle, 10.0. Still need to verify anything else?

Teachers in Grades 6 through 12 must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: four in the license area and four general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment (4 + 4 = 8).

Teachers employed by a local board must have evidence of a rating of at least "proficient" on the most recent annual evaluation to renew. That means a rating of Proficient or higher on three of the five NC Professional Teaching Standards, including Proficient on Standard 4.
If a teacher is not deemed proficient in the final year of a renewal cycle, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan, which leads to an IPL rather than a CPL renewal.

Mandatory training hours count toward CEUs only if the training is required by State law or by a local board as a condition of employment, and the educator has otherwise met the renewal requirements for the license type.

question: Out-of-state teacher with 7 years of experience in Georgia, now applying for NC. Holds a valid GA professional license. How many years of experience count toward the NC license?
context_ids: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

claims.text: An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a continuing professional license (CPL); an applicant with fewer than three years may qualify for an initial professional license (IPL).

For a CPL, the applicant must hold a clear license from another jurisdiction, meaning one that is in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, not revoked or disciplined, not under a pending unprofessional-conduct investigation, and not voluntarily surrendered during an investigation.

For a CPL, the applicant must also either hold NBPTS certification or have a licensure system substantially similar to NC's. Substantially similar means the other jurisdiction required, at minimum, completion of a recognized educator preparation program and a passing score on an out-of-state exam for each license area sought.

For a standard NC CPL, a teacher needs at least three years of licensed teaching experience, but the NC-specific CPL rule (LICN-024) applies to holders of an NC IPL or residency license. The out-of-state pathway is LICN-025 §2.

Under the out-of-state IPL pathway, an applicant in Elementary Education or Special Education: General Curriculum must meet NC exam requirements by the end of the third year of licensure. Applicants in other areas must either pass the out-of-state exam for that area or meet NC exam requirements before or during the third year, having attempted them in the first year.

The experience-counting rules in LICN-006 (one year for six calendar months of full-time work in a fiscal year, with part-time and partial years combinable) determine creditable experience for salary purposes for NC public school employees. They do not state how out-of-state experience counts toward an NC license.

Arithmetic under LICN-006 §I(a): if the 7 Georgia years were each at least six calendar months of full-time work in a school unit, they would total 7 years of salary experience credit. This depends on how the policy applies to out-of-state service, which the passages do not state.
Service as a tutor, clerical paraprofessional, or substitute teacher is not recognized as professional educator experience credit.

question: Teacher on an IPL has 3 years of experience at 0.5 FTE and 2 years at 1.0 FTE. How do those years count?

answer.summary: For salary experience credit, the 2 years at 1.0 FTE should count as 2 years if each is a full fiscal year of full-time work, and each 0.5 FTE year can count as 1 year (3 years total) only if it is a full fiscal year at 15 or more hours per week and is not excluded work. Hours per week, fiscal-year timing, and the type of work must be confirmed before a final count is given.

claims.text: Full-time work in a school unit of at least six calendar months within one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30) earns one year of experience credit.

A calendar month is the number of days employed divided by the number of days in the pay period, multiplied by the employee's percentage of employment. A full 12-month fiscal year at 0.5 FTE therefore equals 12 × 0.5 = 6 calendar months of full-time-equivalent experience, which meets the six-month threshold.

Part-time work requires a minimum of 15 hours per week to establish experience credit in a school unit. One year can be earned if the experience totals six calendar months of full-time experience in a single fiscal year.
The passages do not define what FTE means in hours per week, so they do not confirm whether a 0.5 FTE position meets the 15-hour weekly minimum.

Partial years of full-time or part-time experience can be combined for credit. Two years of part-time work can make one year if they equal six months of full-time experience. Partial full-time years can be combined with other partial years to equal one year.

Assuming the 0.5 FTE years each meet the 15-hour minimum and span a full fiscal year, the arithmetic is 3 years × 6 FTE-equivalent months = 3 years of credit. The 1.0 FTE years add 2 years × 12 months = 2 years of credit, for a total of 5 years.

Service as a tutor, clerical paraprofessional, or substitute teacher is not recognized for professional educator experience credit. Experience credit is not awarded for leave of absence periods, except as required by workers' compensation or USERRA.

Experience credit for a single year served in two or more school administrative units is allowed unless the State Board has been advised that the contract was willfully breached during the school year.
The IPL provisions in the passages set licensure qualifications, but they do not state whether the license type changes how salary experience credit is calculated.
For a CPL, an applicant must have at least three years of licensed teaching experience, but the passages do not define how that licensed experience is counted or whether these years qualify.

question: Teacher got a CPL 6 years ago and has never renewed. Do they have to start fresh or is there a grace period?

answer.summary: The passages do not provide a grace period for a CPL that was not renewed. The available paths are a validation request by the employing PSU, which depends on whether the teacher was employed by any PSU in the preceding fiscal year, or, if the license expired and the teacher is not validated, an application for an IPL once the notice of expiration is received. The analyst needs to confirm the teacher's employment history and the details below before an outcome can be given.

claims.text: A CPL is a five-year renewable license, and each teacher holding a CPL must renew it every five years.

Teachers in Grades 6 through 12 must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: four in the license area and four general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Teachers in PreK through Grade 5 also complete eight CEUs, split three in license area, three literacy, and two general. The grade band therefore determines the required breakdown, though the total is eight either way.

A teacher employed by a local board must have evidence of a rating of at least 'proficient' on the most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL, defined as Proficient or higher on three of five Professional Teaching Standards including Standard 4.

If a teacher is in the final year of a renewal cycle, was not deemed proficient, and holds a current CPL, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan. If the teacher is placed on the plan and otherwise meets requirements, DPI issues an IPL.

If a teacher meets the Section 1 criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan by the employing LSAU, the license expires at the end of the renewal cycle. The teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving notice of expiration from DPI.

A PSU governing body may request that DPI validate an expired CPL even without the requisite CEUs, but only if the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year. A validated CPL is effective for three years, and the educator must complete the LICN-030, LICN-031, or LICN-032 renewal requirements by the end of the third year to renew for a new five-year cycle.

Validation is therefore available only through the employing PSU and only if the educator had no PSU employment in the preceding fiscal year. If the teacher was employed by a PSU in that year, the passages do not describe validation as an option.
The passages do not contain a grace period for an unrenewed CPL, and they do not state whether a lapsed CPL must be restarted from an IPL. The 'start fresh' framing is not addressed directly.

A CPL held six years without renewal is past one five-year cycle, so it has likely expired. The passages do not give the exact expiration date, which depends on the issue date and renewal cycle details the analyst has not provided.

question: Candidate has 5 years of public school teaching in Tennessee and wants a NC Continuing Professional License. Which path applies and what do they still need?

The passages do not say whether the candidate's Tennessee license is clear or what the candidate's grade band and license areas are.

claims.text: A continuing professional license based on possession of a clear license in another jurisdiction must meet the requirements of LICN-025.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a CPL. The candidate's 5 years of teaching is more than 3 years (5 > 3), so the experience threshold is met if the 5 years were licensed professional educator experience.

The Tennessee license must be a clear license, meaning it is in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, has not been revoked or disciplined, has no pending unprofessional-conduct investigation in any state, and has not been voluntarily surrendered while under investigation.

The applicant must also either hold a National Board for Professional Teaching Standards certification, or show that the other jurisdiction's licensure requirements were substantially similar to North Carolina's. Substantially similar means the applicant had to complete a state-recognized educator preparation program and pass an out-of-state exam.

A passing score on the applicable exam is required for each license area for which the applicant seeks licensure under LICN-010. LICN-010 is not among the passages, so the required exams and scores cannot be confirmed.
NBPTS certification, if held, is credited with all eight CEUs for the renewal cycle in which it is received, and renewal of NBPTS certification earns two CEUs.

Once licensed, the CPL must be renewed every five years. Renewal requires eight CEUs per cycle: for Grades 6-12, four in the license area and four general; for Pre-K-5, three in the license area, three literacy, and two general.

Teachers employed by a local board of education must have a rating of at least 'proficient' on the most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL. That requires 'Proficient' or higher on three of five standards, including Standard 4.

The out-of-state path (LICN-025) does not mention the Beginning Teacher Support Program. The BTSP exemption for three or more years of licensed teaching outside North Carolina appears in the LICN-024 §1 teacher path. The passages do not say whether that exemption applies to the LICN-024 §3 path.

The 3-year experience also falls short of the out-of-state CPL threshold of more than three years, so the analyst should confirm the experience count and the other facts listed before advising.

claims.text: NC CPL renewal requires CEUs earned in each five-year cycle. Teachers in Grades 6-12 must complete 8 CEUs: 4 in the license area and 4 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Teachers in Pre-K through Grade 5 must complete 8 CEUs: 3 license-area, 3 literacy, and 2 general. The grade band therefore determines the required breakdown.

A professional educator may receive CEUs through college or university credit or through professional development programs. The policies do not state whether professional development completed outside the United States, including UK PD, is accepted as CEUs.

For an out-of-state applicant to qualify for a continuing professional license, the applicant must have more than three years of licensed professional educator experience. An applicant with exactly 3 years does not meet that threshold as written.

An out-of-state applicant must also hold a clear license from the other jurisdiction, meaning it is in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, not revoked or disciplined, has no pending unprofessional-conduct investigation, and was not surrendered under investigation. A UK license must be checked against each of these criteria.

The applicant must either hold National Board certification or show that the other jurisdiction's requirements are substantially similar to NC's. Substantially similar requires completion of a state-recognized educator preparation program and a passing score on the applicable exam for each license area sought.
A teacher employed by a local board of education must have evidence of a rating of at least proficient on the most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL.

The passages do not describe UK licenses or UK credentials directly. Under the policies, an out-of-state credential is assessed under the out-of-state clear-license criteria rather than being treated as an NC CPL.

For an NC continuing professional teacher license from an NC IPL, the applicant needs at least three years of licensed teaching experience and must complete a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless the applicant has at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina. Three years of UK teaching experience may therefore satisfy that exemption if it is licensed teaching experience.

If the applicant is on an international faculty license, that license is issued at the A-Level with zero years of experience for State Salary Schedule purposes, regardless of prior experience, and cannot be converted to another license until it expires.

question: Holds a Permit to Teach, has a bachelor's, wants to teach two more years. Can the permit be renewed?

answer.summary: A Permit to Teach cannot be extended or renewed under LICN-017 §2. It is valid only until June 30 of the fiscal year for which it was requested, so teaching for two more years would require a different license type, which the passages do not establish for this educator.

claims.text: A permit to teach is valid until June 30 of the fiscal year for which it was requested, and a permit to teach cannot be extended or renewed.

A permit to teach may be requested by a public school unit only for an applicant who holds at least a bachelor's degree and has never been issued any other North Carolina professional educator license.

Because the permit cannot be renewed, the educator's ability to teach beyond the current fiscal year depends on obtaining a different license classification; the passages do not say which one, or whether this educator qualifies for one.

question: Candidate wants an emergency license for a math vacancy. Eligible?

answer.summary: The candidate may be eligible for an emergency license only if the governing body requests it, the candidate holds a bachelor's degree with at least 18 credit hours of coursework relevant to math, has not completed a recognized EPP in math, and does not qualify for a residency license. The passages do not give the candidate's degree, math coursework, EPP history, or residency eligibility, so those facts must be confirmed before deciding.

claims.text: Under LICN-018 §1, the governing body of a public-school unit may request an emergency license for an applicant under its employment only if the applicant meets all three conditions: holds at least a bachelor's degree including at least 18 credit hours of coursework relevant to the licensure area for which the applicant was hired, has not completed a recognized EPP in that licensure area, and does not qualify for a residency license.
A person who holds or previously held a residency license is not eligible for an emergency license in the same license area.

Residency eligibility requires either at least 24 hours of coursework in the content area for which the license is sought, or passing the applicable licensure examination for that content area. If the candidate meets either test, the candidate would qualify for a residency license and would not be eligible for an emergency license under LICN-018 §1(c).

An emergency license is valid until June 30 of the fiscal year for which it was requested and cannot be extended or renewed. The general definition describes an emergency license as a one-year nonrenewable license, which is consistent with a one-year term but does not fix the end date.

For State Salary Schedule pay, an emergency license is set at the level of a bachelor's degree (A-Level) teacher license. The candidate may qualify for graduate degree pay or experience pay under LICN-006, which is not in the passages.
Under LICN-013 §3(b), DPI shall not add additional teaching license areas to an emergency license, so the emergency license covers only the area for which it is issued.

The passages do not state the grade band of the math license area. The math classifications listed in LICN-010 §6(a)(v) and §6(a)(vi) are K–6 add-ons that cannot stand alone. The passages do not say whether a secondary math position is a separate license area or how it is classified.

question: A teacher with a BS in English is teaching Spanish I on a lateral basis for the rest of the year. Is that allowed and for how long?

answer.summary: The passages do not support a current "lateral" arrangement: lateral entry licenses were repealed, and only people who held one before repeal get special treatment. The likely options are a permit to teach (valid only to June 30 of the requested fiscal year, not renewable), a limited license, or a residency license, and the choice depends on facts you have not given, such as whether the teacher has ever held an NC professional license and whether the teacher has 24 Spanish coursework hours or has passed the Spanish exam. Emergency license eligibility and the duration of limited and residency licenses are not in the passages.

claims.text: The passages do not describe a current lateral entry pathway. Lateral entry licenses under G.S. 115C-297 were repealed by S.L. 2017-189, and the policies address only individuals who previously held one and did not convert it before it expired.

Spanish is a recognized license area in the policies, both as a secondary area (Grades 9-12) and as a special subject (Kindergarten-Grade 12), so the analyst must determine which area the teacher's license would be issued under for Spanish I.

A permit to teach may be requested by the governing body of a public school unit for an applicant who holds at least a bachelor's degree and has never been issued any other North Carolina professional educator license. A BS in English satisfies the degree element, so the teacher's licensing history determines eligibility.

A permit to teach is valid only until June 30 of the fiscal year for which it was requested and cannot be extended or renewed. If the rest of the year falls within one fiscal year, the permit would end at that June 30 and could not carry into the next year.

A limited license may be requested for a teaching license area (not administrator or student services areas) if the applicant meets the requirements of G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(4a). The passages do not spell out those statutory requirements or the license's duration.

A residency license may be requested if the applicant meets G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(5) and has either completed at least 24 hours of coursework in the content area or passed the applicable licensure examination for that area. A person who holds or previously held a residency license cannot be eligible for a permit to teach or emergency license in the same area.

A residency license holder requires the employing unit to provide at least 3 hours of field experience before classroom teaching and 10 hours over the first year, plus 10 days of professional development (which may be split 5 preservice and 5 during the first year).
An emergency license is issued at bachelor's-level (A-Level) pay, but the passages do not state the eligibility requirements or the license term for an emergency license.
The IPL option requires completion of EPP requirements in NC, which the teacher's described background does not indicate.

question: Teacher earned NBPTS certification in 2019. License expires next year. Does the national board cert affect renewal?

answer.summary: NBPTS certification gives full credit for all eight CEUs, but only for the renewal cycle in which the certification was received. Whether the 2019 certification helps this renewal depends on which five-year cycle 2019 falls in and whether the certification was renewed since. The policies also still require the evaluation standard for renewal.

claims.text: A teacher who receives NBPTS certification receives credit for all eight CEUs, for the renewal cycle in which the certification is received.
A teacher who renews an NBPTS certification receives credit for two CEUs, for the renewal cycle in which the certification is renewed.
A renewal cycle is the five-year period between each renewal of a CPL, and a teacher with a CPL must renew every five years.

If the 2019 certification falls in the cycle that ends with the upcoming expiration, the eight-CEU credit applies to this renewal. If it falls in an earlier cycle, the policies do not show it carrying forward, so the teacher would need other CEUs or a renewal of the NBPTS certification in the current cycle (two CEUs).

The teacher must still have evidence of at least a proficient rating on the most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL, and must meet the CEU requirements for their grade band. NBPTS credit does not waive the evaluation requirement.
A license expires on June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire, unless it is renewed, extended, or converted.
CEUs may be earned through college or university credit or professional development programs.

question: CPL renewal due in June. Has 7 CEUs. Good to renew?

answer.summary: As stated, 7 CEUs is one short of the 8 that a teacher must complete per renewal cycle, so the CEU count alone does not support renewal. Whether the renewal can proceed depends on the teacher's grade band, the CEU category breakdown, the most recent evaluation rating, and whether the teacher is in the final year of the cycle.

claims.text: A teacher holding a CPL must renew it every five years and complete eight CEUs in each renewal cycle.
One CEU equals either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from an institution of higher education, or ten clock hours of professional development programming.
Arithmetic: 8 required CEUs minus 7 completed CEUs leaves a shortfall of 1 CEU.

The eight CEUs must be distributed by grade band. For Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5: 3 CEUs in the license area, 3 literacy CEUs, and 2 general CEUs. For Grades 6 through 12: 4 CEUs in the license area and 4 general CEUs. The 7 CEUs must be checked against the category requirement for the teacher's grade band.

A teacher employed by a local board of education must have evidence of a rating of at least proficient on the most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL. This means a Proficient or higher rating on three of the five NC Professional Teaching Standards, including Proficient on Standard 4.

If the teacher is employed by a local board, holds a current CPL, is in the final year of the renewal cycle, and was not deemed proficient, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan. If placed and otherwise eligible, DPI issues an IPL. The plan lasts 90 instructional days in low-performing schools and 60 instructional days in other schools.

If a teacher meets the Section 1 criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan, the license expires at the end of the renewal cycle. The teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving the DPI expiration notice.
Every license expires on June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire, unless it is renewed, extended, or converted under SBE policy.
A teacher who receives National Board Certification receives credit for all eight CEUs for that cycle. A teacher who renews National Board Certification receives credit for two CEUs for that cycle.
A General Assembly member is exempt from the teacher CEU requirements for a renewal cycle in which the member serves, if the member notifies DPI during that cycle.

What grade band does the teacher serve (Pre-K through Grade 5 or Grades 6 through 12)? Which CEUs have been completed in each category?
Is the teacher employed by a local board of education (LSAU)?
What were the teacher's most recent annual evaluation ratings, including whether Standard 4 was rated Proficient and whether at least three standards were rated Proficient or higher?
Is June the final year of the current five-year renewal cycle? Was the teacher placed on a mandatory improvement plan?
Does the teacher hold National Board Certification, or is the teacher a General Assembly member?
Are the 7 CEUs already completed, or are some still in progress? Are they expressed in CEUs or in clock hours or semester hours?
not_covered: What happens to a renewal that is one CEU short when the teacher is not on a mandatory improvement plan. The passages say only that the license expires if the teacher meets the Section 1 criteria but is not placed on a plan, and that a 2(b)(iii) IPL path requires the CEUs.
Any grace period, late renewal, or ability to complete the missing CEU after June 30.
The exact renewal-cycle end date for this teacher, beyond the June 30 general expiration rule.
Whether a CEU earned in a category can be counted toward a different category when the category targets are not met.
Any rule about the timing of CEUs earned during the cycle.

question: Applicant from Georgia, 2 years of teaching, needs NC license. What do they qualify for?
context_ids: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

answer.summary: With two years of licensed teaching experience, this Georgia applicant appears to fit the out-of-state threshold for an Initial Professional License (IPL), but not yet for a Continuing Professional License (CPL), which requires more than three years. The outcome depends on whether they hold a clear Georgia license in the corresponding area or completed a recognized EPP, their degree level, and their exam results.

claims.text: An out-of-state applicant with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for an initial professional license, if they either hold a license in the corresponding license area in another jurisdiction or completed an educator preparation program recognized by the jurisdiction where the EPP is based.

Under LICN-020, an applicant who holds a clear out-of-state license and has fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction also qualifies for an IPL, and an out-of-state EPP completion qualifies as well. Two years is under the three-year threshold in both policies.

Exam requirements for an out-of-state IPL depend on the license area. For Elementary Education or Special Education: General Curriculum, the applicant must satisfy NC licensure exam requirements by the end of the third year of licensure regardless of any out-of-state exam. For other areas, the applicant must either pass an out-of-state exam for that area or satisfy NC exam requirements before or during the third year, having attempted them at least once in the first year.
Out-of-state exam results must be presented at the time of initial NC licensure, and out-of-state exam results cannot be used to convert an IPL to a CPL.

A CPL for an out-of-state applicant requires more than three years of licensed professional educator experience, plus a clear license (in good standing, renewable, with no revocation, discipline, pending unprofessional-conduct investigation, or surrender under investigation). The applicant must also hold NBPTS certification or have requirements substantially similar to NC's, including an recognized EPP and a passing out-of-state exam for each area sought. With two years of experience, this applicant does not yet qualify for a CPL.

The highest license level depends on the highest degree level at which the applicant completed an EPP (Bachelor's A, Master's M, Specialist S, or Doctoral D). The applicant is only eligible for a license at that highest level.

If the applicant has a bachelor's degree, has never been issued any NC professional educator license, and an NC public school unit employs them, that unit may request a permit to teach. The permit is valid until June 30 of the fiscal year requested and cannot be extended or renewed.
The fee table lists an Out-of-State Initial Professional License at $100 for applications opened effective January 1, 2017.
citations: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

question: Teacher's CPL lapsed three years ago. Taught four years before that. What's the reinstatement process?

answer.summary: The policies provided do not contain a reinstatement process for a lapsed CPL. The outcome depends on why the license lapsed and on the teacher's employment in the preceding fiscal year, so the analyst should confirm those facts before choosing between an IPL application and a PSU-requested validation.

claims.text: When a teacher meets the renewal criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan by the employing LSAU, the license expires at the end of the renewal cycle, and the teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving notice of expiration from DPI.

The governing body of a PSU may request that DPI validate an expired CPL, even without the requisite CEUs, but only if the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year. A validated CPL is effective for three years, and the educator must complete the renewal requirements in LICN-030, LICN-031, or LICN-032 by the end of the third year to renew for a new five-year cycle.

The facts given do not say whether the teacher was employed by any PSU in the preceding fiscal year. If the teacher was employed by a PSU in that year, the validation route in LICN-033 §3 is not available.

The only reinstatement provision in the passages (LICN-007 §8) applies to a license that was revoked or an application that was denied under LICN-007. A petition may be filed no sooner than 12 months after the revocation or denial, in writing to the Superintendent, and the Superintendent may deny, grant, or grant on probation. This provision does not address a license that simply lapsed or expired.
The residency license reinstatement provision (LICN-019 §2(b)) applies only to residency licenses, so it does not apply to a CPL.

If the teacher later seeks a CPL again, the passages require holding an initial professional educator license or residency license in North Carolina, at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and completion of a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless an exception applies. An exception applies to an applicant with three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina, or one who previously held a CPL that reverted to an IPL under LICN-030.

question: Teacher has an Initial Professional License in elementary ed and wants the EC general curriculum add-on. Doable?

question: CTE welding instructor, 8 yrs industry. Cert?

answer.summary: Welding is a recognized CTE license area (Trade and Industrial Education – Welding), and it does not appear in the required-testing table. The passages do not state the credentials needed for that license, so the answer depends on the educator's degree, license history, and whether the 8 years of industry work meets the experience criteria. For salary purposes, the 8 years could count for up to 8 years of credit if earned after a bachelor's degree, or 4 years if earned before one.

A permit to teach requires at least a bachelor's degree and that the applicant has never been issued any other North Carolina professional educator license. The permit is valid only until June 30 of the fiscal year requested and cannot be extended or renewed.

For salary purposes, non-teaching work experience can be credited only on the recommendation of the LEA's designated personnel administrator, and only if it is relevant to the area of licensure and meets the criteria: at least half-time (20 or more hours per week), completed after age 18, not on-the-job training, and paid and documented.

Experience credit rate: one year of credit for every two years of full-time relevant non-teaching experience completed before the bachelor's degree; one year of credit for every year completed after the bachelor's degree. Partial years can be combined.

For Class V Career-Technical Trade and Industry Education licenses, one year of credit is awarded for every year of relevant non-teaching experience completed after the individual has finished the training and work experience required for the provisional license. The passages do not define those provisional-license requirements.

Continuing professional license requirements, if the educator already holds an initial license, include at least three years of licensed teaching experience, a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless an exception applies, and satisfying licensure exam requirements. Whether this applies depends on the educator's current license status, which is not known.

question: PTT expired 2 months ago. Can they reinstate?

A validated CPL is effective for three years, and the educator must then complete the renewal requirements by the end of the third year to renew for a new five-year cycle.

question: Teacher on a limited license for a special subject, 3 years in. Can they keep renewing it?

answer.summary: A limited license for a special subject can be renewed under the policies if the employing unit certifies the teacher is currently employed, effective, and being encouraged to pursue a CPL, and the teacher meets expected EVAAS growth where data exists. claims.text: A limited license is a three-year renewable license issued to an individual who has completed an EPP but has not satisfied the applicable licensure examination requirements.

To renew a limited license, the PSU governing body employing the licensee must submit an affidavit, signed by the supervising principal and the local superintendent, attesting that the licensee is currently employed by the PSU, is an effective teacher, and that the PSU will encourage the licensee to pursue a CPL.

To renew a limited license, the licensee must meet or exceed expected growth as measured by EVAAS, where such data is available. If there is more than one year of growth data, DPI averages it. Data is limited to the years since the limited license was first issued or its most recent prior renewal, and DPI does not consider EVAAS data from 2019-2020 or 2020-2021.
Every license expires on June 30 of the year it is set to expire unless it is renewed, extended, or converted under SBE policy, so the limited license must be renewed by that date to remain valid.
